layering.description: auth_router.py imports Types/Config/Repository/Service only (no UI). Frontend: authStorage.ts is Config-layer (no upward imports); client.ts (api/) reads it to attach the bearer token; useAuth.ts (service/) is the only caller of authApi.ts; RouteGuard.tsx is pure/presentational, taking auth state as props rather than calling useAuth() itself.

typing.description: mypy --strict clean on all of backend/src; frontend tsc --noEmit clean. No Any/any usage.

folder_structure.description: api/routers/auth_router.py, api/schemas/auth_schemas.py exist with tests/integration/test_auth_login_api.py; auth_service.py gained hash_password/verify_password; schema.sql seeds 3 demo users (csr_jane/admin_raj/dealer_priya). Frontend: config/authStorage.ts, api/authApi.ts, service/useAuth.ts, ui/components/RouteGuard.tsx, ui/pages/LoginPage.tsx all exist with matching test files; App.tsx calls useAuth() exactly once and passes state down as props (not called independently in RouteGuard/LoginPage).

env_vars.description: No new environment variables — reuses E1-S4's existing jwt_secret_key/jwt_algorithm/jwt_expiry_minutes.

migrations.description: schema.sql's users table seed grew from empty to 3 demo rows (csr/admin/dealer), applied idempotently via the existing INSERT OR IGNORE pattern — not a new migration mechanism.

test_checks.description: Valid seeded staff credentials (CSR, ADMIN) return HTTP 200 with an access_token whose decoded claims carry role and subject.
A subscriber mobile number with no prior registration returns a pre-registration token (subscriber_id: null); after registration, login returns the populated subscriber_id.
Invalid staff credentials (wrong password or unknown username) return HTTP 401 with an identical, generic reason code and response shape in both cases.
Exactly one seeded demo user per CSR/ADMIN/DEALER role exists after schema apply, with password_hash populated via a real PBKDF2 hashing function (never plaintext, salted, verifiable).
A login attempt, successful or failed, never logs the raw password or an unmasked mobile number.

A subscriber JWT issued by the real login endpoint for subscriber A is rejected with 403 when used against an endpoint scoped to subscriber B's data (this is the migrated E1-S4 test, now exercising a real-issued token rather than a test-minted one — no separate AC-6 test was written, per the generator's report, since this migration already proves it end to end).
A login page calls POST /api/auth/login, stores the returned token, and the API client attaches it as a bearer token on subsequent calls.
test_checks.command: cd frontend && npx vitest run tests/LoginPage.test.tsx tests/useAuth.test.tsx

test_checks.description: A role-based route guard renders the fallback (login page) when unauthenticated or when the current role isn't in the allowed set, and renders children otherwise.
test_checks.command: cd frontend && npx vitest run tests/RouteGuard.test.tsx

test_checks.description: The migrated E1-S4 and E3-S3 integration test files, which now obtain tokens through the real login endpoint instead of minting them directly, still pass in full — proving no regression was introduced into already-evaluator-approved Group B/D work.
test_checks.command: cd backend && uv run pytest -q tests/integration/test_auth.py tests/integration/test_plan_api.py
test_checks.expected: 20 passed (8 from test_auth.py, grew from 7 to accommodate the real-subscriber seeding this migration needed; 12 from test_plan_api.py, unchanged — both verified via separate isolated runs before writing this contract)

note_for_evaluator: This is a fix-loop evaluation, not a normal story group: it closes the auth-login gap found during Group E's evaluation. grp-e1s6-09-regression-check is the most important entry here — verify it carefully, since test_auth.py and test_plan_api.py were already evaluator-approved in Groups B and D and this story modified their token-acquisition mechanism.
